instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Admit You Need Me
cards.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That cupboard leans exactly like your first one. I thought my lesson about checking the back panel had stuck.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got the instructions this time. I don't need another lesson.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good progress. Which page says to leave the door leaning against the wall?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just hold the door while I fit the hinges?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's the useful bit of my lesson: asking for help. Try that request again without 'just.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought a blanket. You remembered my heater-reset lesson, but not my lesson about keeping yourself warm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can fix the heater. Leave the blanket; I am freezing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent diagnosis. Now can you say you still need a little help from the person who taught you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need you to tuck the blanket round me while I work. You can leave the switches to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's better. I'll do the tucking; you can practice that sentence whenever you get cold without me.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm sending you off with soup and warm bread. Before your train, taste the soup; let's see what you learned about seasoning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt. There, I learned something. Coat, please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly. A cook checks the correction too. One more taste after I salt it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, it's right now. I've got ten minutes to reach the station.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your bread needs wrapping first. Fold this cloth with me; I clearly left transport out of your cookery lessons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're using my old packing method. Almost. Let me wrap that jam before you zip the case.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already wrapped in my jumper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your train jumper. I did teach you to keep something warm within reach. We'll have to unpack it.

beats.text: I'll leave the jam here. Problem solved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to simplify. Now taste it before you decide what to leave behind; I'll get two spoons.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your usual mug out. I taught you that tea can follow a difficult conversation, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are we having a difficult conversation? You look cross.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're noticing faces now. What could you say before I pour?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly. Keep 'I'm sorry' and start again from there. You don't need to describe my feelings; I already have them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parents arrive in ten minutes. This would be a good time to use the apology I taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I sent you a thumbs-up. I thought we'd sorted it.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send a sad face, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your face is right here. Put a sentence beginning with 'I' under it before the doorbell goes.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've invited six people to dinner. You used to panic over two; my hosting lessons have brought you a long way. Is six all right?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still only have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You're checking numbers before menus, just as I taught you. I'll borrow the extra seats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And cook? I'm not feeding six people while you collect chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do both. You can practice the welcome I taught you. Does that make the invitations a yes?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember my lesson about giving a garden one focal point. Can we agree the pond should be ours?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have a tree, not a pond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're comparing the options. I've had the tree removed; now you can judge the space properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You cut it down before asking me? The stump is still there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good eye for unfinished work. Can you approve removing the tree now, so I can tell the grinder to finish what we agree was the right start?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your lettering's finally ready for more than bin labels. Eighty wedding place cards could show what my lessons gave you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like the lettering. I don't want to copy eighty names or argue with your aunt about purple ink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll read the names and handle my aunt. You could finally use that purple flourish I spent weeks teaching you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Without you correcting every capital letter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep my pen capped. You can make the guests wish I'd taken lessons from you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've outgrown the tool drawer I taught you to organize. Sorting this shed could give you a whole workshop of your own.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Until you dump paint tins over everything again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the final lesson: make the teacher obey the labels. You could set every shelf's rules.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Including one you're forbidden to touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Especially that one. Put it at eye level so I have to admire how thoroughly you've learned to keep me out.
